description: Fully inherits stock_alpha_v1 and adds quality constraints related to turnover, traded amount, VWAP, prior close, and high-range acceptance.

schemas.name: Volume Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses changes in trading participation as confirmation of whether the event has external participation support.

terms.Trading Participation: The scale of market participation represented by volume, traded amount, or similar variables.
terms.Confirmation: A supportive relationship where an external variable aligns with the market behavior expressed by the event.

schemas.name: Volume Non-Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses insufficient trading participation or unsynchronized trading changes as quality evidence that the event lacks external participation support.

terms.Trading Participation: The scale of market participation represented by volume, traded amount, or similar variables.
terms.Non-Confirmation: The external variable does not provide synchronized support for the market behavior expressed by the event.

schemas.name: Volatility Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses changes in volatility magnitude or true range as confirmation of whether the event is accompanied by volatility release.

terms.Volatility Magnitude: The state of price-change magnitude, true range, real body range, or return volatility.
terms.True Range: true range, typically characterized by the maximum of high-low, |high-prev_close|, and |low-prev_close|.

schemas.name: Low-Volatility Setup Filter
schemas.description: Requires the event to occur after a low-volatility or contraction backdrop, used to filter for clearer release or regime-switch events.

terms.Low Volatility: The level of price volatility is relatively low versus its own recent state.
terms.Contraction Backdrop: The price range, true range, or real body range has narrowed relative to its recent state.

schemas.name: Range Expansion Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses expansion of the price operating range as confirmation of whether the event is accompanied by an expansion in activity range.

terms.Operating Range: The price range formed by the highest and lowest prices within the observation window.
terms.Expansion: The operating range expands relative to its own recent state.

schemas.name: Sufficient Break Depth
schemas.description: Weights the quality of an event's boundary-crossing behavior based on how far price moves beyond a reference level or boundary.

terms.Break Depth: The distance after price moves beyond a reference level or boundary.
terms.Reference Level or Boundary: A price reference specified by the event or context.

schemas.name: Sufficient Reclaim Depth
schemas.description: Weights the quality of reclaim-type events based on how far price moves back inside a reference level or boundary.

terms.Reclaim Depth: The distance after price moves back inside a reference level or boundary.
terms.Reclaim: Price moves back inside the level or boundary that had previously been crossed.

schemas.name: Anchor Distance Scaling
schemas.description: Applies continuous weighting to an event based on the distance between the event and the context reference level.

terms.Anchor: A price reference level provided by the context.
terms.Distance Scaling: A continuous quality weight based on how close price is to the anchor.

schemas.name: Close Strength
schemas.description: Weights the quality of an event's closing behavior based on the relative position of the close within the current bar or observation window.

terms.Close Position: The position of close relative to the high-low range or the observation-window range.
terms.Close Strength: The extent to which the close is near one side extreme of the range.

schemas.name: Body Strength
schemas.description: Weights the quality of an event's real-body behavior based on the size of the candlestick body relative to its own recent state or the current bar range.

terms.Body Strength: The size of the candlestick body relative to its own recent state or the current bar range.

schemas.name: Wick Noise Filter
schemas.description: Filters or downweights events that are easily affected by single-bar noise based on wick proportion or wick disturbance.

terms.Wick: The part of the high-low range not covered by the open-close body.
terms.Noise Filter: Reduces the weight of events with unclear patterns or larger disturbance.

schemas.name: Path Cleanliness
schemas.description: Weights event cleanliness based on whether the price path is direct and has limited back-and-forth movement.

terms.Price Path: The trajectory of gradual price movement within the observation window.
terms.Cleanliness: The degree to which the path has less back-and-forth movement and noise disturbance.

schemas.name: Chop Filter
schemas.description: Reduces the weight of events occurring in paths with frequent back-and-forth fluctuations and unclear direction.

terms.Chop: Price frequently changes short-term direction within the observation window.
terms.Unclear Direction: Price lacks stable local progression or clear positional change.

schemas.name: Path Efficiency Filter
schemas.description: Retains or weights events with higher path efficiency based on the relationship between net displacement and path length.

terms.Net Displacement: The change from the starting price to the ending price within the observation window.
terms.Path Length: The cumulative magnitude of segment-by-segment price changes within the observation window.
terms.Path Efficiency: The ratio or relationship of net displacement relative to path length.

schemas.name: Freshness Decay
schemas.description: Applies decay weighting to event validity based on the time since the most recent occurrence or confirmation.

terms.Freshness: The closeness of the event to the most recent occurrence or confirmation time.
terms.Decay: Reducing quality weight as time passes.

schemas.name: First-Touch Preference
schemas.description: Prefers events that occur on the first touch of a reference level or condition slice, reducing the weight of repeated touches.

terms.First Touch: The first time price approaches or touches a reference level and forms an event.
terms.Repeated Touch: Price approaches or touches the same reference level multiple times.

schemas.name: Event Cooldown Filter
schemas.description: Downweights or filters frequent consecutive occurrences of the same type of event to reduce repeated-event stacking.

terms.Event Cooldown: Maintaining some interval between same-type events or reducing the weight of consecutive repeats.
terms.Repeated-Event Stacking: Multiple similar events occurring within a short period.

schemas.name: Condition Persistence
schemas.description: Weights event quality based on whether the event or event-context condition persists.

terms.Persistence: The degree to which an event condition remains present across adjacent bars or within the observation window.
terms.Condition: A boolean or continuous state formed by the event, context, or a combination of both.

schemas.name: Short-Lived Pulse Preference
schemas.description: Prefers events that appear suddenly within a short time and do not persist for long, used to filter pulse-type events.

terms.Short-Lived Pulse: An event that appears suddenly and disappears quickly within a short time.
terms.Persistence: The event condition remains present for a long time.

schemas.name: Self-Normalized Magnitude
schemas.description: Uses a variable's magnitude relative to its own historical state to reduce exposure to absolute price, absolute trading activity, or instrument scale.

terms.Self-Normalization: Scaling a variable relative to its own historical distribution, mean, volatility, or quantile.
terms.Scale Exposure: Non-alpha differences caused by differences in instrument price, volume, or contract characteristics.

schemas.name: ATR-Normalized Distance
schemas.description: Uses volatility units to normalize price distance, break depth, or reclaim depth, reducing price-scale differences across instruments.

terms.ATR: Average true range, used to describe the normal scale of price fluctuation.
terms.Normalized Distance: Relative price distance after dividing by volatility scale.

schemas.name: Quantile-Normalized Strength
schemas.description: Uses time-series quantiles or cross-sectional quantiles to characterize event strength, reducing the impact of outliers and scale differences.

terms.Quantile: The relative ranking position of a variable within historical samples or cross-sectional samples.
terms.Strength: The size of event magnitude, depth, distance, trading activity, volatility, or other continuously measurable quantities.

schemas.name: Higher-Timeframe Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses position, state, or similar events on a higher time scale as external confirmation for the current event.

terms.Higher Timeframe: A longer time scale relative to the current bar.
terms.External Confirmation: Supportive information from a different scale or variable.

schemas.name: Cross-Bar Consistency
schemas.description: Uses similar events or similar states across multiple bar granularities to confirm the consistency of the current event.

terms.Multiple Bar Granularities: For example 1m, 5m, 10m, 30m, or other time granularities.
terms.Consistency: Events or states observed at different granularities have similar meaning.

schemas.name: Missing-Data Robustness
schemas.description: Requires event logic to remain robust under missing values, suspension-style gaps, or differences in listing history across instruments.

terms.Missing Values: Observations that do not exist or are unavailable in the data.
terms.Robust Handling: Avoiding abnormal signals, infinite values, or widespread false triggers caused by missing values.

schemas.name: Outlier Clipping
schemas.description: Applies mild suppression to extreme inputs, extreme intermediate variables, or extreme outputs to reduce signal domination by single-point anomalies.

terms.Outliers: Observations that deviate significantly relative to their own history or a reasonable range.
terms.Mild Suppression: Reducing the impact of extreme values through truncation, compression, or smoothing.

schemas.name: Level Acceptance Quality
schemas.description: Evaluates whether an event is accepted by a reference level based on the extent to which price stays near, closes near, or repeatedly confirms that level.

terms.Level Acceptance: A state where price stays near or closes near a reference level, making it an effective trading area.
terms.Reference Level: A price anchor, boundary, or equilibrium area specified by the context or event.

schemas.name: Level Rejection Quality
schemas.description: Evaluates whether an event is rejected by a reference level based on how quickly price leaves it after touching it or fails to stay there.

terms.Level Rejection: After touching a reference level, price fails to stay and moves away again.
terms.Quick Departure: Price moves away from the reference level within a short observation window.

schemas.name: Volume Concentration Quality
schemas.description: Weights event quality based on whether trading participation is concentrated in the event area or key phase.

terms.Volume Concentration: Trading participation is relatively concentrated in a specific price area or time phase.
terms.Key Phase: The phase when the event occurs, breaks, reclaims, touches, or gets confirmed.

schemas.name: Pre-Event Compression
schemas.description: Modulates the quality of an event's preparatory structure based on whether the price range, volatility, or body magnitude narrows before the event occurs.

terms.Pre-Event Compression: Before the event occurs, the price range, volatility, or body magnitude narrows relative to its recent state.
terms.Preparatory Structure: The market background state formed before the event occurs.

schemas.name: Post-Event Expansion
schemas.description: Modulates event quality based on whether the price range, volatility, or body magnitude expands after the event occurs.

terms.Post-Event Expansion: After the event occurs, the price range, volatility, or body magnitude expands relative to the prior state.
terms.Follow-Through Behavior: Market behavior within an observation window after the event occurs.

schemas.name: Range Efficiency
schemas.description: Measures whether volatility produces effective progression using the ratio of net price change to range width.

terms.Range Efficiency: The ratio of abs(close-open) or abs(close-prev_close) relative to high-low or true range.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Quantile-Normalized Strength
schemas.description: Based on the original quantile-normalized-strength semantics, applies cross-sectional rank or percentile to the event or intermediate strength at each timestamp to reduce instrument scale differences.

terms.Quantile-Normalized Strength: Using quantiles to characterize event strength.
terms.Cross-Sectional rank: Ranking instrument scores at the same timestamp.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Neutrality Hint
schemas.description: Retains the original cross-sectional neutrality-hint semantics, requiring implementation to reduce cross-sectional exposure caused by stable differences in instrument scale, price level, or trading activity scale.

terms.Cross-Sectional Neutrality: Reducing exposure caused by stable differences in instrument scale.
terms.Cross-Sectional Exposure: The signal is mainly explained by price, trading activity, or position size.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Volume Confirmation Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original volume-confirmation semantics, compares the strength of trading-participation changes supporting the event across instruments, and ranks or weights them at the same timestamp.

terms.Volume Confirmation: Changes in trading participation support the event.
terms.Cross-Sectional Confirmation Strength: The relative strength of volume confirmation within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Volatility Confirmation Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original volatility-confirmation semantics, compares the strength of volatility release accompanying the event across instruments, and ranks or weights them at the same timestamp.

terms.Volatility Confirmation: The event is accompanied by changes in volatility magnitude or true range.
terms.Relative Volatility Confirmation: The strength of volatility confirmation within the cross section.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Range Expansion Confirmation Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original range-expansion-confirmation semantics, compares the relative strength of price operating-range expansion across instruments.

terms.Range Expansion Confirmation: Expansion of the price operating range supports the event.
terms.Cross-Sectional Expansion Strength: The relative position of expansion magnitude within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Sufficient Break Depth Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original sufficient-break-depth semantics, compares the normalized magnitude by which price moves beyond a reference level or boundary across instruments.

terms.Break Depth: The magnitude by which price moves beyond a reference level or boundary.
terms.Relative Depth: The ranking of normalized break depth within the cross section.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Sufficient Reclaim Depth Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original sufficient-reclaim-depth semantics, compares the normalized magnitude by which price moves back inside a reference level or boundary across instruments.

terms.Reclaim Depth: The magnitude by which price moves back inside a reference level or boundary.
terms.Relative Depth: The ranking of normalized reclaim depth within the cross section.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Path Efficiency Filter Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original path-efficiency-filter semantics, compares efficiency as net displacement relative to path length across instruments, and mildly weights the event by relative efficiency.

terms.Path Efficiency Filter: Retaining or weighting the event based on net displacement relative to path length.
terms.Cross-Sectional Efficiency: The relative position of path efficiency within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Missing-Data Robustness
schemas.description: Based on the original missing-data-robustness semantics, requires panel implementations to handle differences in listing history, missing coverage, and stagnant gaps across instruments, avoiding missingness patterns becoming the main cross-sectional signal.

terms.Missing-Data Robustness: Remaining robust under missing values, stagnant gaps, or differences in listing history.
terms.Missingness Pattern: Instrument differences caused by data unavailability rather than trading logic.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Close Strength Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original close-strength semantics, compares the relative strength of closing position within the current bar or observation window across instruments.

terms.Close Strength: The relative position of the close within the current bar or observation window.
terms.Cross-Sectional Strength: The ranking of closing performance strength at the same timestamp.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Body Strength Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original body-strength semantics, compares the size of the candlestick body relative to its own recent state or the current bar range across instruments.

terms.Body Strength: The size of the candlestick body relative to its own recent state or the current bar range.
terms.Cross-Sectional Body Strength: The relative position of body strength within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Wick Noise Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original wick-noise-filter semantics, compares the relative magnitude of wick proportion or wick disturbance across instruments, and reduces the weight of noisier instruments.

terms.Cross-Sectional Noise: The relative position of noise within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Path Cleanliness Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original path-cleanliness semantics, compares whether price paths are direct and have limited back-and-forth movement across instruments, and weights the event by relative cleanliness.

terms.Path Cleanliness: Whether the price path is direct and has limited back-and-forth movement.
terms.Cross-Sectional Cleanliness: The relative position of path quality at the same timestamp.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Self-Normalized Magnitude Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original self-normalized-magnitude semantics, first normalizes the variable relative to its own historical state, then compares strength across instruments at the same timestamp.

terms.Self-Normalized Magnitude: A variable's magnitude relative to its own historical state.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional ATR-Normalized Distance Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original ATR-normalized-distance semantics, compares price distance, break depth, or reclaim depth after normalization in volatility units across instruments.

terms.ATR-Normalized Distance: Using volatility units to normalize price distance.
terms.Cross-Sectional Distance: The relative position of normalized distance within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Outlier Clipping
schemas.description: Based on the original outlier-clipping semantics, applies mild clipping to extreme cross-sectional inputs, intermediate variables, or outputs at each timestamp to reduce signal domination by a single instrument.

terms.Outlier Clipping: Mildly suppressing extreme inputs, intermediate variables, or outputs.
terms.Cross-Sectional Extremes: Values at the same timestamp that are clearly far from most instruments.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Level Acceptance Quality Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original level-acceptance-quality semantics, compares the relative degree to which price stays near, closes near, or repeatedly confirms a reference level across instruments.

terms.Level Acceptance Quality: Price stays near, closes near, or repeatedly confirms a reference level.
terms.Cross-Sectional Acceptance: The relative position of acceptance degree within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Level Rejection Quality Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original level-rejection-quality semantics, compares the relative degree to which price quickly departs from or fails to stay after touching a reference level across instruments.

terms.Level Rejection Quality: Price quickly departs from or fails to stay after touching a reference level.
terms.Cross-Sectional Rejection: The relative position of rejection degree within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Cross-Sectional Volume Concentration Quality Ranking
schemas.description: Based on the original volume-concentration-quality semantics, compares the relative degree to which trading participation is concentrated in the event area or key phase across instruments.

terms.Volume Concentration Quality: Trading participation is concentrated in the event area or key phase.
terms.Cross-Sectional Concentration: The relative position of concentration degree within the instrument universe.

schemas.name: Turnover Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses changes in turnover rate relative to its own recent state to confirm whether the event is supported by genuine trading participation.

terms.Turnover Confirmation: Changes in turnover_rate form a supportive relationship with the price behavior expressed by the event.
terms.Own Recent State: The stock's turnover-rate level or quantile within its own historical window.

schemas.name: Traded Amount Confirmation
schemas.description: Uses changes in traded amount relative to its own recent state to confirm whether the event is supported by capital participation.

terms.Traded Amount Confirmation: Changes in standardized traded amount form a supportive relationship with the price behavior expressed by the event.

schemas.name: High-Turnover Noise Filter
schemas.description: When turnover rate is extremely high but net price displacement, close strength, or path efficiency is insufficient, downweights the event to avoid mistaking trading crowding itself for effective progression.

terms.High-Turnover Noise: High turnover_rate does not produce proportionate effective price results.
terms.Filter: Reducing the weight of events with heavy input but weak price results.

schemas.name: Traded Amount Efficiency Confirmation
schemas.description: Confirms the input-output efficiency of an event based on the proportional relationship between effective price progression and standardized traded-amount input.

terms.Effective Price Progression: Price outcomes such as net displacement, breakout depth, or directional close.
terms.Traded Amount Efficiency: The relationship between effective price progression and traded-amount input standardized by its own history.

schemas.name: VWAP Hold Persistence
schemas.description: Weights the quality of reclaim and rejection events based on the extent to which price continues to close or stay on the target side after crossing VWAP.

terms.VWAP Hold: After crossing, price continues to remain on the target side of VWAP.
terms.Persistence: The proportion or consecutive length satisfying the hold condition within a finite historical window.

schemas.name: Prior-Close Anchor Acceptance Quality
schemas.description: Weights prior-close anchor interaction events based on the extent to which price closes, stays, or continues to progress on the target side after crossing the prior close.

terms.Prior-Close Anchor: pre_close or act_pre_close consistent with the price adjustment convention.
terms.Acceptance Quality: The extent to which price holds on the target side after crossing and forms effective closes.

schemas.name: High-Range Close Acceptance Quality
schemas.description: Weights high-level acceptance events based on closing strength in the upper quantile of the recent range, persistence of staying there, and drawdown magnitude.

terms.High-Range Close: close is located in the upper-quantile area of its own recent rolling range.
terms.Acceptance Quality: The strength and persistence of the high-range close, and the degree to which subsequent drawdown is controlled.

schemas.name: Opening Gap Robustness Filter
schemas.description: Uses prior close, open price, and recent volatility scale to identify valid gaps, and filters pseudo-gaps caused by adjustment switches, price-limit moves, trading resumption, or extreme anomalies.

terms.Normalized Gap: The distance of open relative to convention-consistent pre_close or act_pre_close, normalized by its own recent volatility scale.
terms.Pseudo-Gap: A jump caused by data anomalies, adjustment handling, or special trading states rather than normal price discovery.
